The research method collects vibration signal data through fiber optic detectors and converts the vibration signal using Fourier transform. At the same time, the collected signals are denoised using ensemble empirical mode decomposition to obtain processed real-time vibration signals. Random neural networks are utilized to identify fiber optic vibration signals and achieve the resolution and warning of abnormal signals. The research results show that the convergence effect of the research model has been effectively improved, and the convergence speed is faster compared to other algorithms. At the same time, the research model has a high recognition accuracy for fiber optic signals, with a signal recognition accuracy of 91.06% -95.41%, which is 2.65% - 23.12% higher than other detection models. The research model can also maintain a low signal recognition error in low signal-to-noise ratio environments, with a reduction of 4.97% -23.64% compared to other algorithms, indicating that the signal detection coverage and accuracy of the research model remain at a high level and can effectively detect the trend of signal changes. Therefore, the design of the research model can validly raise the precision of signal detection and provide a highly accurate detection model for signal recognition of fiber optic sensors.

articleTitle: DLMM-DTI: Deep Learning-Based Mamba Model for Drug-Target Interaction Binary Classification Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Drug–target interactions (DTIs) play a vital role in drug development, as accurately predicting them can speed up discovery and lower costs. However, traditional DTI identification methods are costly and time-intensive, mainly due to the complex nature of molecular and protein spaces. Furthermore, existing deep learning approaches overlook necessary molecular substructure, leading to suboptimal predictive accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose DLMM-DTI, a novel prediction model that integrates BCM, CFM, CNN, and Mamba techniques to capture diverse features of drug and protein fragments. By incorporating multiple representations, DLMM-DTI effectively captures both intra- and inter-model interactions. Experimental results demonstrate that DLMM-DTI outperforms existing methods on Human, Celegans and BIOSNAP datasets, reducing training costs and improving prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of YOLOv8, YOLOv9, and YOLOv10 in Tile Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: The complex and diverse textures on tile surfaces, along with the variety of defect types, pose significant challenges for automated defect detection. Accurately identifying subtle defects and achieving real-time detection are currently hot research topics. Deep - learning methods represented by YOLO have provided opportunities and solutions to this problem, and YOLOv8, YOLOv9 and YOLOv10 are the three most advanced algorithms in the YOLO series at present, showing excellent detection performance in defect detection. Through an in - depth comparative study of the specific performance of these three algorithms in tile defect detection, this paper provides valuable reference for technology selection and application scenarios in the field of tile defect detection, and better balance between detection efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Social-Passing: A New Approach to Trajectory Prediction in Multi-Vessel Scenarios for Sensing Intrinsic Social Information of Vessels
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Currently existing vessel trajectory predictions are predicted for individual vessels. However, due to the complexity of the maritime environment, it’s not feasible to capture the mutual information among vessels. In order to better capture the dynamic interrelationships between vessels at sea, inspired by social pooling and message passing mechanism, we design a Social-Passing mechanism to dynamically update the node information of vessels, and combined with LSTM network, we propose a SP-LSTM model. In our model, we first utilize the LSTM network to extract features from the historical trajectory data of a single vessel. Subsequently, we perform the Social-Passing analysis of the vessels at the current time node, based on the distance range between vessels, to update the information of all current nodes. Meanwhile, since multi-vessel datasets are difficult to collect, we propose an AIS Multi-Vessel Data processing algorithm (AMVD) to process the datasets. Finally, we compare several existing models, and all of our SP-LSTM achieves better performance results.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Efficient On-Star Compression Algorithms for FPGA Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Image compression has always been a hot topic in the field of aerospace. The onboard processing unit, due to its background of deep space operation, has greatly limited performance in terms of data storage and data transmission. Satellite remote sensing images are developing towards larger size, higher frame frequency, and more frequency bands, which increasingly demand storage space and processing power. There is an urgent need for a set of efficient and lightweight image compression hardware and software. Therefore, in this work, we have improved the Context-Based Adaptive Lossless Image Compression (CALIC) algorithm, including error quantization and entropy coding, to meet the requirements for on-orbit processing in terms of compression time and compression ratio. At the same time, aiming at the working scenario of on-orbit processing, we chose Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) as the platform to deploy the improved CALIC and designed the arithmetic coding Av value calculation process in parallel on this basis, which greatly reduced the processing time on the hardware side. We have carried out simulation verification of this paper’s image compression algorithm on the KODAK24 and SZTAKI_Airchange datasets. The experimental results show that our method strikes a good balance between compression ratio and compression rate compared with typical compression algorithms, making it suitable for on-orbit processing scenarios.

articleTitle: Clustering of Drug Side Effects Based on Multi-Omics Data
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: The investigation of drug side effects is of paramount importance for identifying and predicting potential risks associated with pharmacological interventions, thereby enhancing patient safety and optimizing therapeutic outcomes. In-depth analysis of side effect data establishes a robust scientific foundation for drug optimization, personalized treatment strategies, and drug repurposing. With advancements in technology, researchers can now access multi-source biological data spanning diverse scales and levels. This study introduces the Integration of Multi-Omics Data for Drug Side Effect Clustering (IMOD-DSEC) model, an unsupervised learning framework designed to cluster drug side effects by integrating multi-omics data through a heterogeneous graph. The proposed model systematically generates meaningful node embeddings, harmonizes dimensional disparities, and facilitates effective clustering. Specifically, the model begins by generating semantically rich embeddings for each node based on its descriptive attributes, which are processed through a denoising autoencoder to ensure dimensional consistency. Two modules are then designed to aggregate multi-omics data through both intra- and inter-node type learning. The first module employs a Bi-LSTM model to refine the embeddings within nodes of the same type. The second module uses a random walk with restart strategy to sample highly correlated heterogeneous neighbor nodes for each central node, applying an attention mechanism to update the central node’s representation and produce the final embeddings. The k-means algorithm is subsequently used for clustering. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of IMOD-DSEC in accurately clustering multi-system drug side effects, underscoring its potential as a valuable tool for advancing drug safety research and multi-omics data integration.

articleTitle: Sensitive Image Recognition based on Improved Channel Distillation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: With the swift development of Deep Learning (DL) techniques, Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable performance in image recognition. However, they still encounter various challenges in sensitive image recognition. In the absence of extensive and well-annotated datasets, these methods may be prone to overfitting and could exhibit unstable output responses during the classification process. Moreover, the current mainstream deep learning models have a considerable number of parameters and are difficult to deploy on the embedded side. To solve this problem, this paper firstly conducts a comprehensive evaluation of three mainstream distillation model architectures, namely knowledge distillation, joint training, and channel distillation. Secondly, we further improve the channel distillation model, optimize the network structure, incorporate a random image generation approach to enhance the model's generalization capability, and employ a weighted cross-entropy loss function to boost the accuracy of complex image recognition. The experimental results indicate that channel distillation demonstrates the best recognition performance on sensitive image datasets. The proposed improvement strategy effectively reduces overfitting and improves the classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhanced Real-time Pavement Damage Analysis: Integrating CNN Edge Detection with YOLO for Accurate Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: As urban road damage issues become increasingly severe, automated road damage detection systems are becoming critically important. This paper proposes a CNN-YOLO-based road damage detection model aimed at enhancing the accuracy of road damage detection. Our model optimizes the identification process for cracks and potholes by integrating image resizing, minimum filtering, edge detection, and deep learning techniques within a multitask learning framework. Initially, we employ a minimum filter for image resizing to improve detection speed and reduce processing time. Subsequently, by converting the images to grayscale and utilizing YOLO for object recognition, the accuracy of detection is significantly enhanced. Edge detection techniques, including the Laplacian filter, are used to extract road damage features, ensuring accurate identification of various damage types, including longitudinal cracks, transverse cracks, network cracks, and potholes. Our proposed method leverages the rapid scanning capability of the YOLO model and the feature learning ability of CNN to achieve efficient damage detection.Experimental results show that the model achieves over 90% accuracy across different datasets, with outstanding performance on P-SNR and SSI-M metrics, reaching 50.2 dB and 0.84, respectively. This indicates that the proposed CNN-YOLO model offers high accuracy and reliability in detecting road damage. Additionally, the model demonstrates fast computation speed during training and adapts well to various data conditions and damage types.

articleTitle: Multi-Kinect Spinal Motion Measurement Method Based on Markings
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Three-dimensional spinal motion measurement is of great significance in fields such as rehabilitation medicine, sports science, and biomechanics. At present, optical motion capture systems are abundant, among which Vicon and OptiTrack are commonly used for three-dimensional motion measurement of the spine. Although they have high accuracy, they are expensive and occupy a large space, which limits their widespread application in outpatient screening. As a low-cost, easy-to-use, and highly reliable depth sensor, Kinect has the potential for three-dimensional motion measurement of the spine. The marker based multi-Kinect spine motion measurement method introduces marker points and multi-perspective data registration techniques, aiming to solve the problem of unmarked bone recognition being unable to describe changes in spine morphology, as well as the limitation of a single camera being unable to capture six degrees of freedom motion data of the spine. The final outcomes of the experiment made a validation of the accuracy of the method in evaluating spinal morphology (average MED of 2.7mm) and six degree of freedom motion data (average RMSE error of 3.7mm). This method not only ensures measurement accuracy, but also significantly reduces cost and operational complexity, and has broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Dehazing Algorithm Based on Image Illuminance
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an image illuminance-adaptive defogging algorithm, aiming to address the issues of image distortion and inadequate consideration of diverse lighting environments inherent in traditional methods, thereby enhancing the algorithm's universal applicability. The algorithm initially refines the image through superpixel segmentation, subsequently detecting point light sources precisely and estimating the overall illumination conditions, providing a precise environmental basis for the defogging process. Based on the acquired illuminance information, defogging parameters are adjusted to achieve defogging tailored to varying lighting conditions. To further elevate the visual quality of defogged images, this algorithm integrates the Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) technique with the point light source detection mechanism, enhancing image contrast while maintaining a natural appearance and minimizing noise amplification. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to conventional methods, the proposed algorithm achieves notable improvements in key evaluation metrics such as Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) across foggy images under diverse lighting conditions, effectively enhancing the quality of defogged images.

articleTitle: PF-UNet: A Short-term Precipitation Correction Model Integrating Multiple Meteorological Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: The short-time precipitation correction is to correct the forecast deviation of the numerical model by integrating the actual observation data. Previous precipitation correction methods based on deep learning mainly used a single precipitation element to correct the forecast data, and failed to fully consider the impact of other meteorological elements on short-term precipitation process. However, the precipitation process is coupled by many meteorological elements in its formation and evolution, resulting in its complexity and variability. Therefore, considering the influence of other meteorological factors in the correction process can better improve the accuracy of short-term rainfall forecast. In this paper, a deep learning network PF-Unet is proposed to correct the short-term precipitation of multiple factors. The PF-Unet model integrates the key features of various meteorological elements, strengthens the influence of meteorological elements on the generation and evolution of precipitation events, and improves the accuracy and reliability of short-term precipitation forecasting. The experimental results show that the precipitation area and precipitation size of the PF-Unet model with multi factors are closer to the global precipitation measurement (GPM) data. This study further improves the accuracy of the numerical prediction system in short-term precipitation prediction.

articleTitle: High-Precision Terrain Modeling of Tailing Ponds Using UAV LiDAR Point Cloud Data
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: This study proposes a high-precision methodology for dry beach extraction and safety parameter calculation in tailing ponds using UAV LiDAR data. Leveraging the Difference Consistency Iterative Closest Point (DICP) algorithm, this approach achieves precise point cloud registration, while an improved progressive morphological filtering method effectively separates ground and non-ground points. Bilinear interpolation is further applied to address data gaps, enhancing data completeness and terrain continuity. The resulting Digital Elevation Model (DEM) exhibits high spatial resolution and minimal elevation error, meeting the precision requirements of engineering applications. This method demonstrates the viability and efficiency of UAV LiDAR technology for detailed terrain monitoring and safety assessment in tailing pond environments. The study concludes with a discussion on optimizing these techniques for complex terrains and exploring their potential applications in broader environmental monitoring contexts.

articleTitle: Leveraging AI for Superior Corrosion Resistance in Industrial Application
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: In the highly competitive cigarette manufacturing industry, adhesive systems are crucial yet vulnerable components often exposed to corrosive environments, leading to rapid material degradation and increased maintenance costs. This study leverages machine learning to accelerate the development of novel corrosion-resistant alloys tailored for these harsh operational conditions. By employing an an explainable random forest algorithm, we optimized alloy compositions to maximize corrosion resistance while maintaining mechanical integrity. Comprehensive electrochemical testing and real-world simulations demonstrated that the newly developed alloys outperform traditional materials, particularly in chloride-rich and fluctuating pH environments. Our findings highlight the transformative potential of AI-driven material design in enhancing the efficiency, durability, and cost-effectiveness of industrial machinery, setting a new benchmark for integrating intelligent technologies in material science. This research not only extends the lifespan of critical machine components but also paves the way for future innovations in smart manufacturing systems.

articleTitle: Nodeseq2vec: Node Sequence Representation Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Current network representation learning techniques focus on mapping each network node to a low-dimensional space, essentially functioning as node representation learning approaches. In this paper, we introduce a novel method for network representation, called node sequence representation learning, which shows highly competitive performance compared to traditional node representation approaches. We develop two scalable frameworks, nodeseq2vec and nodeseq2vec++ aim to project each node sequence generated from a network to a low-dimensional space inspired by distributed representations of documents. Therefore, the node se17quences which may represent a research field, a cooperative group, etc., on network are computable. The nodeseq2vec framework is able to learn high-quality node sequence feature representations through modeling the relationship between a node sequence and all the nodes it has. The nodeseq2vec++ framework further combines semantics with structure in net- work with external text information. In our experiments, we design two methods to approximately represent node features through multiple node sequences, and we comprehensively evaluate our framework against existing network representation models on various real-world datasets across different domains. Ultimately, we achieve significantly improved performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods in both multi-label classification and citation recommendation tasks.

articleTitle: Transmission-Lines Foreign Objects Detection Using MSYOLO
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Foreign objects detection on transmission lines has the problems that the accuracy is low due to the images captured by UAVs often have small targets, and most models can hardly meet the requirements of real-time detection. Thispaper proposes a novel multiscale-adaptive YOLO-based network model with SIoU loss (MSYOLO) for precise detection of foreign objects on transmission lines. First, an enhanced scale-aware pyramid network which combined dual focus feature aggregation network and a unified feature enhancement module was proposed to improve the detection rate of small targets. Second, SIoU and Fast NMS was introduced to further correct and accelerate the bounding box regression. Experimental results show that our proposed method reaches 86.65 AP50, 46.22%AR and 149 FPS, which is superior to the other anchor-based methods of YOLO series.

Author Keywords: Foreign objects detection on transmission lines

articleTitle: MFP-CNN: Multi-Scale Fusion and Pooling Network for Accurate Scene Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Scene classification presents significant challenges in computer vision, crucial for advancements in robotics and automation. These challenges include intra-class variation, varying object sizes, and spatial information diversity. To address these issues, this paper proposes MFP-CNN, a Multi-Scale Fusion and Pooling Convolutional Neural Network [37]. We introduce a Lightweight Multi-Stage Feature Fusion (LMSFF) method to effectively capture multi-scale information and enhance feature discriminability, thus mitigating intra-class diversity. We incorporate Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP) to improve scale invariance by considering features at various spatial scales. Additionally, we use the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism to focus on informative regions, resulting in improved feature extraction and accuracy. We also introduce the Scene7 dataset, which features diverse real-world scenes with annotations for both scene classification and object detection. Extensive experiments on custom and public datases validate the effectiveness of MFP-CNN, achieving an impressive top-1 accuracy of 97.4% on Scene7, surpassing state-of-the-art methods. Notably, our model achieves this with a parameter-efficient design, utilizing only 2.13MB for trained parameters. MFP-CNN offers an efficient and impactful solution for scene classification, advancing robot vision applications. Access the source code and dataset at https://github.com/Wanelle/MFP-CNN.

articleTitle: Space Crowdsourcing Allocation Scheme Based On Improved Fishing Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: This study proposes a mobile crowdsourcing task allocation method based on the Improved Fishing Optimization Algorithm (ICFOA-SCAM), aiming to address the issue of user preferences and waiting time being overlooked in existing crowdsourcing platforms, thereby improving user satisfaction. Optimizing task allocation has become the key to improving service quality. The ICFOA-SCAM method comprehensively considers the personalized preferences of users, the abilities of workers, and the spatiotemporal characteristics of tasks. By defining key concepts such as spatiotemporal units, user preference evaluation scores, waiting time evaluation scores, and user satisfaction evaluation scores, it enriches the definition of tasks and crowdsourcing authors, enabling the model to more comprehensively consider the complexity of spatial crowdsourcing task allocation. The experimental results show that the ICFOA-SCAM method outperforms traditional white whale optimization algorithm and grey wolf optimization algorithm in terms of user satisfaction and task allocation efficiency. ICFOA-SCAM improves the global search capability and convergence speed of the algorithm by introducing Singer chaotic mapping initialization and Lévy flight strategy. The contribution of this article lies in proposing a new crowdsourcing task allocation model, which not only improves the efficiency and quality of task allocation, but also enhances user satisfaction. Future research will explore how to leverage workers' social relationships to further enhance the effectiveness of task allocation, as well as improve the service quality and user satisfaction of crowdsourcing workers while protecting location and information privacy.

articleTitle: Lightweight object detection for UAV Images based on multidimensional attention fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) image object detection holds broad application prospects in environmental protection, remote sensing, intelligent transportation, and many other fields. However, drone-captured aerial images present challenges such as small targets, low resolution, and limited device power consumption, which pose significant demands on the precision of object detection and the lightweight nature of algorithms. This paper proposes an improved lightweight object detection method tailored for drone-captured aerial images. To better extract the features of small objects, a C2fCF module is introduced into the backbone component, and a C2fMDAF module is introduced into the neck component. Experimental results show that the lightweight object detection method proposed in this paper can significantly improve the accuracy of object detection while almost not affecting the detection efficiency.

articleTitle: Script Event Prediction Based on Large Model Reflection Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Script event prediction (SEP) involves predicting the most plausible next event given a sequence of historical events. This paper introduces ReGen-SEPM (Reflection and Generation for Script Event Prediction Model), a framework combining LLaMA-based generation and a reflection mechanism to improve prediction quality. The generative module produces initial predictions based on context and prompts, while the reflection module evaluates and refines them for semantic consistency and causal plausibility. A self-supervised learning mechanism further enhances the reflection module's effectiveness. Experiments on the New York Times Corpus show that ReGen-SEPM outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in accuracy, semantic similarity, and causal coherence, with ablation studies highlighting the contributions of reflection and self-supervised learning.

articleTitle: Exploring Semantic Links in Bibliographic Network-based Citation Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Citation recommendations hold substantial academic importance in the era of big scholarly data. The tasks not only depend on the semantic expression of publications, but also are associated with structural information. Recently, many recommendation tasks have been modeled using network-based representations, where nodes signify entities and edges indicate their interactions. Creating node representations with fusing both semantic and structural information in network and considering citation recommendation as publication node similarity searching task is an effective solution. In order to achieve this goal, existing works consistently interact two publications. This paper addresses this challenge by introducing semantic links within a bibliographic network for citation recommendations. The basic motivation is to construct semantic links on network instead of the role of keywords. The semantic links denote two publications sharing similar semantic meanings and provide valuable supervision to learn publication representations. To obtain high-quality semantic links, we create them on network with high-similarity other publications' text representations captured from the two-level hierarchical and transparent information (word-sentence-document). This word-sentence-document information reflects the hierarchical structure of publication texts, accurately capturing their semantics. Finally, we verify the effectiveness of semantic link in bibliographic network-based citation recommendation using two real-world datasets.

articleTitle: An Attribute-Based Signature Scheme with Flexible Access Control on Lattice
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Attribute-based signatures (ABS) is a powerful cryptographic solution that provides fine-grained access control while improving flexibility and usability. This innovative approach allows generating and verifying digital signatures without revealing private information about the signer, thus maintaining user anonymity. Traditional ABS schemes usually rely on simple threshold structures, which make it difficult to support complex access control policies, have limited flexibility, and the computational complexity of generating and verifying signatures can be high, especially when dealing with a large number of user attributes. We propose a novel ABS scheme that incorporates more flexible access control mechanisms to overcome these limitations. Our approach utilizes secret sharing techniques to construct an access tree where user attributes are efficiently mapped to the leaves of the tree. This design supports a variety of logical operations, including "AND", "OR", and "threshold" gate structures, which enable sophisticated access policies. In addition, our scheme builds on the small integer solution (SIS) problem to ensure robust anonymity and adaptive unforgeability of selected information. This is achieved by selecting access tree structures and attribute sets under the Randomized Oracle Model (ROM) that conform to the defined access structure. The proposed ABS scheme not only enhances the security and privacy of digital signatures, but also improves the efficiency, which is a valuable contribution to the field of cryptographic access control.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm for Icon Detection in Vehicle Dashboard
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Icon detection in vehicle dashboard is a crucial step in the automated testing of vehicular systems. However, the lack of publicly available datasets for the vehicle dashboard, Automated testing has high real-time detection requirements, combined with existing YOLO (You Only Look Once) models exhibit limitations in detecting small targets effectively, and In practical engineering applications, using camera to capture the vehicle dashboard for icon detection may lead to issues such as strong reflections from ambient light sources, resulting in bright strip and striping. These phenomena hinder existing algorithms’ ability to achieve rapid and accurate detection of vehicle dashboard icons. To address these challenges, this paper constructs a new dataset specifically for car dashboard icon detection, including images of automobile dashboards captured under conditions with strong reflections, bright strips, and stripes, which are challenges commonly encountered in real engineering applications, thus filling the gap created by the lack of suitable existing datasets. Additionally, this work enhances the existing YOLOv8 model by proposing the YOLOv8-ABC feature extraction algorithm, which improves the network’s capability to detect display icons by clustering all anchors in the training set with an improved K-means++ algorithm. This approach yields 12 anchors tailored to the in-vehicle system icon dataset, replacing the anchor-free module in the original model. This approach reduces the number of parameters in the model, which reduces the computational complexity, making the model more suitable for practical engineering applications. Meanwhile, by incorporating BiFPN (Bi-directional Feature Pyramid Network) and CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) into the model, the efficiency of the model is ensured while significantly improving the detection accuracy and improves the detection ability of the model for small targets. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to the original YOLOv8 model, the YOLOv8-ABC algorithm proposed in this paper improves mAP50 and mAP50-95 by 2.8% and 2.6%, respectively, while significantly reducing the number of parameters required by the model. These improvements indicate that the improved algorithm is able to detect icons in vehicle dashboards in real-time with improved detection accuracy, and thus can be effectively applied to automated testing of vehicle dashboards.

articleTitle: Generation of Atrial Fibrillation Electrocardiogram and Atrial Fibrillation Classification Based on BiLSTM-CNN Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: In the medical field, data acquisition and sharing are facing severe challenges, which are mainly attributed to the high sensitivity of medical data and strict access restrictions. In order to resolve the issue, researchers have explored a variety of de-identity methods to promote data sharing, but these methods are sometimes inadequate in protecting personal privacy. Given this, the study in question focuses on using Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) to generate realistic medical time series data, aiming to create a data solution that can protect privacy and meet the needs of research. The purpose of this study is to generate atrial fibrillation signals that accurately reflect the characteristics of normal electrocardiogram (ECG) waveforms. The generated synthetic time series data is expected to serve as an effective substitute for real patient data, thus facilitating its wide application in the medical field without compromising privacy. In order to achieve this goal, this paper uses a variety of GAN architectures to perform deep learning and generation of atrial fibrillation ECG. Subsequently, the authenticity and reliability of the generated data are quantitatively analyzed by three evaluation metrics to ensure its applicability in real-world applications. At the same time, integrating the generated synthetic data into the training set of the AF classifier has resulted in a significant improvement in the performance of the AF classifier. In summary, this paper not only demonstrates the potential of GAN for generating realistic medical time series data, but also the proposed method can be extended to simulate real ECG waveforms of other types of cardiovascular diseases.

articleTitle: Pixel Image Segmentation of Cerebral Hematoma Based on U-Net and Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage is a disease with high fatality rate, and the expansion of hematoma caused by hemorrhage is one of the factors leading to poor prognosis. Fast and accurate segmentation of the contours of cerebral hematoma will help doctors to make diagnosis to a large extent. In order to solve the problem of insufficient precision of U-net segmentation, pixel image segmentation based on U-net and clustering is proposed. The CT images are divided into multiple channels by preprocessing, and on this basis, the cluster is processed twice, and then they enter the improved U-net network respectively. Finally, multiple results are fused to obtain the final segmentation result.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised Balanced Distribution Adaptation Model for Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are essential for safeguarding modern network infrastructures against a wide range of cyber threats. However, the development of highly effective IDS models is often constrained by the limited availability of labeled data for training, as well as the issue of distribution shift when applying models across different network environments. To overcome these challenges, we present a semi-supervised balanced distribution adaptation (SSBDA) transfer learning method for detecting and preventing network intrusion, which learns from limited labeled data and predicts unlabeled data with different distributions. The proposed method first employs the maximum mean discrepancy measure the differences between the marginal and conditional distributions of both the source and target domains. The Hilbert-Schmidt independence criterion is then utilized to estimate the dependence between labels and features within the source domain. To further enhance the model’s generalization ability, manifold regularization is applied to preserve the data’s locality structure. Finally, the processed data is used to train a tri-training classifier. The SSBDA is compared with several well-known transfer learning-based models using the KDDCup99 and NSL-KDD data sets. The experimental results demonstrate that SSBDA outperforms the comparison models in terms of accuracy and F-score, highlighting its superior performance in intrusion detection tasks.

articleTitle: Research On Lightweight Human Fall Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: YOLOv8 has achieved good results in the fall detection task, but there are still some problems with a large amount of computation. Based on this, this paper proposes a lightweight human fall detection algorithm CPDS-YOLO. Firstly, to reduce the number of parameters and the running time of the model, a new CSPPC is proposed to replace C2f based on the lightweight PC(PartialConv). This modification significantly reduces the computational cost and number of model parameters while enhancing detection speed. Secondly, an efficient Partial Self-attention module (PSA) is utilized to enhance the global representation learning ability of the algorithm and improve the model detection precision at a low computational cost. Then, an ultra-lightweight and efficient dynamic sampler (DySample) is designed, which significantly improves the detection accuracy. Finally, the lightweight Slim-Neck replaces the original feature fusion layer, which can reduce the computational cost and effectively fuse the feature information of different stages. Experimental results show that, compared with the original YOLOv8n on the Fall Detect dataset, the precision of the improved fall detection algorithm is increased by 2.8% and the computational cost (GFLOPs) is reduced by 22%, which proves the effectiveness of CPDS-YOLO.

articleTitle: A Context-Aware Intelligent Educational Recommender System Incorporating User Behavioural Knowledge Graph and Causal Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: With the advent of the digital age, the importance of personalized recommendation systems in the field of education has become increasingly prominent, especially in addressing the issues of information overload and difficulty in selecting learning resources. This study proposes a Context-Aware Intelligent Education Recommendation System (SAIERec), which integrates user behavior analysis, knowledge graph reasoning, and causal inference techniques to provide learners with accurate personalized learning resource recommendations. The system construction is based on an in-depth theoretical foundation, including context-aware recommendations and personalized recommendation research based on in-depth knowledge reasoning.By introducing deep learning technology, the system enhances its perception of complex educational contexts and uses knowledge graphs to improve the interpretability of recommendation results. The key construction path of the system covers the initialization of heterogeneous information networks of user behavior, semantic extension of situational knowledge in knowledge graphs, optimization of recommendation algorithms, enrichment of learning resources, and dynamic adjustment of personalized learning paths. In addition, the system uses an attention-based graph convolutional neural network for deep information mining and improves the accuracy and fairness of the recommendation system through counterfactual causal inference strategies. Experimental results show that the SAIERec system outperforms existing recommendation models on multiple datasets, verifying its effectiveness and application potential in the field of education.

articleTitle: MsCAFE-Net: Muti-Scale Contextnal Attention Feature Enhance Network For Skin Lesion Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: A new model for skin lesion segmentation is proposed in this paper, named multi-scale contextnal attention feature enhancement network (MsCAFE-Net) to segment skin lesions to overcome the challenges of confusing factors, contrast changes, irregular shapes, and other factors. By taking full advantage of the multi-scale context, semantic, and spatial information in an image, MsCAFE-Net can achieve better results. Firstly, a multi-scale attention feature selection module (MAFS) is proposed, which can properly gather the spatial information of different scale features by fusing the multi-scale attention mechanism, and reduce the interference of hybrid factors on model judgment. Secondly, a fine-grained deep noise filtering module (FDNF) is designed to effectively filter the noise in the jump connection by fusing the global contextual semanteme info,to enhance the model's sensitivity to targets with irregular sizes and shapes. Finally, a hierarchical feature enhancement module (HFE) is proposed to achieve finer grained feature enhancement by enhancing the feature expression of low contrast samples. The extensive trial results demonstrated that our approach outperforms other leading methods, with our model attaining an accuracy of 96.95%, a Dice score of 92.28%, and a Jaccard index of 85.68%.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Campus Scenic Intelligent Car System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of technology, intelligent vehicle systems are widely used in various fields. In the campus environment, the traditional method of obtaining scenery information is inefficient and lacks real-time performance. This system integrates technologies such as path planning, obstacle avoidance, and cloud visualization, aiming to provide a new method for obtaining and displaying campus scenery information. The system can autonomously plan paths, avoid obstacles, take photos, and upload them to the website platform in real time through cloud visualization technology, providing users with convenient services for viewing scenery information.

articleTitle: A color image channel fusion encryption scheme combining a four-dimensional chaotic system
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Compared with other forms of information communication, images have the advantages of high information density, strong visualization, strong emotional transmission, and cross-linguistic and cross-cultural. It can quickly convey a large amount of information, trigger emotional resonance, cross the language barrier and enhance memorization, which is an efficient way of information transmission. With the wide application of technologies such as social media, smart surveillance and biometrics, images cover a large amount of personal privacy and sensitive information. Image leakage or misuse may lead to serious consequences such as identity theft, privacy violation and even property loss. Currently, many image encryption algorithms encrypt RGB channels independently when encrypting color images. This method, although concise and clear, has some limitations. For example, it may leak the color distribution between channels, and lack of resistance to statistical attacks, and other defects. In summary, this paper proposes a channel fusion encryption scheme combined with a four-dimensional chaotic system to make up for the above limitations. The scheme is organized in three main parts: channel fusion, diffusion encryption and substitution encryption. First, the RGB channels from the original color image are fused into a sequence. Second, the sequence is subjected to diffusion encryption and substitution encryption respectively. The entire encryption model combines four-dimensional chaos and SHA-256 to increase the safety and robustness for the proposed method. After analyzing the safety, the scheme can efficiently realize the image encryption and effectively protect the privacy of the image.

articleTitle: MRPVT: A novel Multiscale Rain-cutting and Pooling Vision Transformer model for Object Detection on Drone-captured Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Drone imagery analysis is an essential part of smart city construction and management. Object detection in UAV images has been a popular research topic recently. The images captured by drones usually have huge scale changes due to the flying and shooting at different altitudes, which puts a burden on traditional deep learning networks. The Transformer-based network has proven successful in computer vision tasks due to its strong long sequence memory analysis capabilities. This article will design a network for object detection and analysis of drone images based on the Transformer structure. The main challenge with using transformers is the high computational cost of processing image sequences, so the common method is to use local attention instead of global attention and a hierarchical structure to compensate for the loss of global vision. However, the large amount of information lost caused by using local attention can not be made up for with this action simply. This paper analyzes the ideas of multiscale and hierarchical structure concepts and attention mechanisms, and embeds multiscale concepts into the local attention structure to further make up for the global view information lost. In order to achieve this, we used the pooling concept to build multiscale pooling layers combined with a pyramid structure and applied it to the multi-head self-attention module. At the same time, we precut the image features entering the pooling block to reduce the length of the image token sequence. While reducing the calculation amount of the vision transformer, the global visual field information is increased as much as possible to obtain better contextual features. On VisDrone dataset, MRPVT as a backbone achieves 47.98% AP50 and 25.20% AP75 accuracy and on UAVDT’s car category achieves 98.84% AP50 and 89.27% AP75 accuracy. As expected, MRPVT delivers great performance on drone-captured images’ object detection and visual aesthetic assessment.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multimodal Named Entity Recognition via Entity Span Detection and Graph Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Multimodal Named Entity Recognition (MNER) focuses on utilizing multiple modalities, including text and images, to recognize specific types of entities within text. Despite recent advancements, existing methods still face several challenges: (1) How to create a unified representation that connects and integrates different modalities, and (2) how to better interact between different modalities based on the unified representation while fully capturing both intra-modal and inter-modal information. In order to address these challenges, we design a new model, enhancing multimodal named entity recognition via entity span detection and graph networks (GENT-Net), which leverages entity recognition and graph networks to enhance MNER. Specifically, we employ a graph-based structure to model text and images, use a graph attention network for multimodal fusion, and introduce entity span detection using a graph convolutional network to assist the MNER task. We perform comprehensive experiments on the publicly available datasets, Twitter2015 and Twitter2017, showcasing the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: YOLOOI: YOLO with Robustness to Outliers and Illumination
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Aluminum is a crucial component in modern society, widely used in fields such as transportation and manufacturing. It is characterized by its light weight, high strength, electrical conductivity, and corrosion resistance, making accurate assessment of its production quality highly significant. In industry, accurately identifying surface defects has become a mainstream task. Currently, defect detection on aluminum surfaces is generally based on image analysis. This strategy is cost-effective compared to other approaches and can leverage well-established technical methodologies. However, in real-world applications, variations in imaging results caused by different lighting conditions, along with unpredictable specular highlights, lead to a decline in detection performance. These challenges, combined with the interference from anomalous points, prevent existing methods from meeting practical needs. To address these issues, we propose the YOLOOI network, which incorporates an original Texture Emphasize and Supplement module (TES) for cross-scale feature fusion and a novel lighting-decoupling data augmentation strategy to eliminate the misleading effects of outlier spots. Our YOLOOI effectively handles variations in lighting conditions and mitigates interference from anomalous points. Experimental results demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms existing models on the aluminum surface defect dataset, highlighting the value of our work and its potential for further development in the future.

articleTitle: Tomographic Object Detection by Unsupervised Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: This work introduces clustering to electrical tomography (ET) and first compares the effectiveness of different unsupervised clustering categories in tomographic object detection. First, the one-step linear back projection (LBP) algorithm is applied to reconstruct a rough image. Then, clustering is introduced to detect and refine the objects in the image, and a higher-quality image is obtained based on the clustering results. Six unsupervised clustering algorithms belonging to different categories, including K-means, Mini Batch K-means, Agglomerative, density peak clustering (DPC), statistical information grid (STING), gaussian mixture model (GMM), are compared from the aspects of clustering evaluation index, reconstruction quality and reconstruction efficiency. Simulation was carried out based on a capacitively coupled electrical resistance tomography (CCERT) system to collect the projection data under the cases of one to three objects to be detected in the sensing region. The research results show that the quality of object detection and reconstruction can be effectively improved by post-processing the image with clustering. It is found that for the single-object distribution, the grid-based clustering algorithm STING provides images with the highest quality. While for the multi-objects distributions (two or three objects), the Agglomerative algorithm belonging to the hierarchy clustering category shows advantage in achieving good images. Concerning the real-time performance, Agglomerative clustering algorithm is also preferred with less computational time than most of the other clustering algorithms. Therefore, among the combinations investigated in this work, LBP + Agglomerative clustering has the overall best performance in topographic object detection, in regarding of the reconstruction quality and efficiency.

articleTitle: Efficient Identity-Based Proxy Blind Signature Scheme over Lattices
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: In response to the issues of low security and computational efficiency in current lattice-based proxy blind signature systems, a novel identity-based proxy blind signature scheme utilizing lattices is proposed. This scheme integrates the user's identity information through matrix accumulation operations to serve as the verification public key, simplifying the identity validation process and strengthening both security and privacy measures. The user's private key as well as the proxy signing key are produced through the extended algorithm of the left sampling algorithm, while the rejection sampling algorithm is employed to produce the proxy blind signature. These enhance the space utilisation of keys and signatures. Moreover, the scheme's security is reducible to solving the small integer solution problem, thereby attaining resilience against one-more unforgeability under the adaptive chosen-message attacks within the random oracle model. Compared to other schemes, our scheme features smaller key and signature sizes, resulting in greater efficiency.

articleTitle: A Review of Human-Object Interaction Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Human-object interaction (HOI) detection plays a key role in high-level visual understanding, facilitating a deep comprehension of human activities. Specifically, HOI detection aims to locate the humans and objects involved in interactions within images or videos and classify their specific interactions. The success of this task is influenced by several key factors, including the accurate localization of human and object instances and the correct classification of object categories and interaction relationships. This paper systematically summarizes and discusses the recent work in image-based HOI detection. First, the mainstream datasets involved in HOI relationship detection are introduced. Furthermore, starting with two-stage methods and end-to-end one-stage detection approaches, this paper comprehensively discusses the current developments in image-based HOI detection, analyzing the strengths and weaknesses of these two methods. Additionally, the advancements of zero-shot learning, weakly supervised learning, and the application of large-scale language models in HOI detection are discussed. Finally, the current challenges in HOI detection are outlined, and potential research directions and future trends are explored.

articleTitle: An Improved Lightweight CNN_BiLSTM Model for Network Intrusion Detection Using the UNSW-NB15 Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: The attack behavior in the network poses a threat to security and privacy issues. In order to improve the effectiveness of IoT network attack detection and compensate for the shortcomings of traditional machine learning methods in detection capabilities, a network intrusion detection method based on lightweight convolutional neural networks (CNN) and bidirectional long short-term memory networks (BiLSTM) is proposed. This method preprocesses data through normalization techniques, extracts data features from both spatial and temporal dimensions using CNN and BiLSTM models, and inputs the extracted spatiotemporal feature vectors into the CNN BiLSTM upper classifier for training, achieving intrusion detection. The proposed model was validated on the dataset UNSW-NB15, and the results showed that the binary and multi classification accuracy of the CNN_BiLSTM model was around 93%. Compared with other methods, the proposed method significantly improves the accuracy of network intrusion detection, and also demonstrates better performance in detection accuracy and false positive rate.

articleTitle: Global-Local Medical SAM Adaptor Based on Full Adaption
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: Visual language models (VLM) have made great breakthroughs in natural image segmentation, and they show consistently high-quality zero-shot transferring capability in many down-stream tasks with prompt engineering. The help of modern parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques, such as low-rank adaption (LoRA) and Medical SAM adaptor (Med-SA) further enables VLM to be well transferred to medical domains. Regardless of the performance, these methods choose to fine-tune VLM in a local manner, where adapters are specified to adapt some layers vital to the down-stream tasks, making them separated by frozen layers in forward path and lack of collaboration in back-propagation. To resolve this problem, we present a global adaption technique and create a novel global medical SAM adaptor (GMed-SA), which can adapt SAM in a collaborative adaption manner. Specifically, all adapters communicate via fully connected layers as a unified sub-network, enabling them to work collaboratively in fine-tuning. We further combine GMed-SA and Med-SA to propose a global-local medical SAM adaptor (GL-Med-SA) for 2D melanoma segmentation dataset. The extensive experiments show that the combined method GL-Med-SA slightly improve the segmentation performance on the challenging publicly available 2D melanoma dataset while only enlarging minor trainable weight parameters and outperforming several state-of-the-art methods in both Dice metrics and Intersection over union (IoU), which demonstrates its superiority.

articleTitle: A review of cross-modal 3D point cloud semantic segmentation methods based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computer, Vision and Intelligent Technology (ICCVIT)
abstract: 3D point cloud semantic segmentation is an important frontier problem in the field of computer vision. It has a wide range of practical applications, especially in the fields of autonomous driving and robot perception. In recent years, the rapid development of deep learning technology has made cross-modal data fusion an effective means to improve the accuracy of point cloud semantic segmentation, especially the combination of point cloud data and visible light images. This fusion method can effectively cope with various challenges in complex environments. This paper takes cross-modal 3D point cloud semantic segmentation as the research background, discusses the fusion mode of visible light images and point cloud data, introduces and analyzes the existing fusion schemes in detail, and introduces the advantages and disadvantages of different fusion schemes and fusion efficiency. Then, this paper introduces the commonly used 3D point cloud semantic segmentation datasets and evaluation criteria. Since point cloud data can be extended to different data forms and is crucial to the fusion efficiency of modal fusion, this paper classifies the current mainstream algorithms according to different forms of point cloud data and discusses their efficiency. Finally, the future development direction of this field is prospected.
